result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.katz_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get Katz centrality for each node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L16397-L16525){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.katz_centrality( alpha=0.1, beta=1.0, max_iter=100, tol=1e-06, attr_name=None, return_dict=False ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Katz centrality measures node influence based on the number of walks of all lengths reaching the node, with walks weighted by `α^length`: `x = α · Aᵀ · x + β` where α is the attenuation factor, `Aᵀ` is the transpose of the adjacency matrix, and `β` is a bias vector (constant for all nodes). For directed graphs, this counts incoming paths, making it suitable for measuring "prestige" or "influence received". Key differences from other centralities: - PageRank: uses teleportation and out-degree normalization - Eigenvector: only considers infinite-length walks (principal eigenvector) - Alpha centrality: uses `A` instead of `Aᵀ` (outgoing vs incoming) - Katz: weights walks by path length, considers all finite walks ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [alpha]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.1]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Attenuation factor for walk lengths. Must be smaller than the reciprocal of the largest eigenvalue (typically < `0.2` for safety). Higher values give more weight to longer paths. [beta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Bias/weight added to each node. Acts as a 'free' centrality that every node gets. Higher values reduce the relative importance of network position. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of iterations for convergence. [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence tolerance threshold. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name for the node attribute to store results. If not provided, auto-generates name from method name (`katz_centrality`). [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary of results. If `False`, stores results as node attributes and returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to normalized Katz centrality scores. If `return_dict=` is `False`: returns self for method chaining. Scores sum to `1.0`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - for undirected graphs, Aᵀ = A, so behavior is similar to alpha centrality - for directed graphs, high Katz = many incoming paths (prestige/authority) - alpha should be < 1/λ_max to ensure convergence (typically α < 0.2) - beta = 1.0 treats all nodes equally; adjust to bias certain nodes - normalizes final scores to sum to 1.0 for interpretability ## Examples {.doc-examples} Calculate Katz centrality on a simple directed graph: ::: {#5f53a8a4 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node("A") .add_node("B") .add_node("C") .add_node("D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "D") .add_edge("A", "D") ) katz = graph.katz_centrality(return_dict=True, alpha=0.1) # D has highest Katz (receives edges from A and C via B) ``` ::: Compare different alpha values: ::: {#0fa02590 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") .add_edge(source="C", target="D") .add_edge(source="A", target="D") ) katz_local = graph.katz_centrality(return_dict=True, alpha=0.05) # Emphasis on short paths katz_global = graph.katz_centrality(return_dict=True, alpha=0.15) # Include longer paths ``` :::
